questions.prompt: Under the CAP theorem, when a network partition occurs between two database regions, what trade-off must a distributed system make?

options.text: Choose between Consistency (linearizability) and Availability
Choose between Durability and Latency
Disable TLS encryption to recover throughput
Switch from TCP to UDP

questions.explanation: During a partition (P), a distributed system must either reject/block requests to preserve Consistency (CP) or serve potentially stale data to maintain Availability (AP).

rubric.label: Distinguishes CP vs AP behavior under partition

questions.prompt: When migrating a high-traffic monolith to microservices, which pattern minimizes big-bang risk by incrementally routing endpoints to new services?

options.text: Big-Bang Cutover
Strangler Fig Pattern
Singleton Proxy
Shared Database Polling

questions.explanation: The Strangler Fig pattern incrementally intercepts and migrates vertical slices behind a routing layer while keeping the legacy system operational.

questions.prompt: An order service must atomically persist an order in PostgreSQL and publish an OrderCreated event to Kafka without dual-write inconsistencies. Which pattern solves this reliably?

options.text: Fire-and-forget Kafka publish before DB commit
Transactional Outbox with CDC or relay poller
Client-side retry loop without idempotency keys
Two-phase commit across browser and Kafka

questions.explanation: Transactional Outbox writes the domain row and outbox event in the same local ACID transaction; a relay/CDC publisher then emits to Kafka with at-least-once delivery.

questions.prompt: Select ALL strategies that make an asynchronous webhook consumer safe under at-least-once delivery.

options.text: Idempotency key stored with a unique constraint
Deduplication window keyed by event ID
Assuming network packets never duplicate
State-machine transition guards

questions.explanation: At-least-once delivery requires idempotent handlers backed by unique keys, deduplication, and valid state transitions.

questions.prompt: Which trade-off is the primary downside of introducing CQRS with an eventually consistent read model?

options.text: Reads become slower than complex multi-join writes
Users may briefly observe stale reads immediately after a write (read-your-writes lag)
Horizontal scaling of read replicas becomes impossible
SQL databases cannot be used on the write side

questions.explanation: Separating write and asynchronously projected read models introduces eventual consistency lag that UX/APIs must handle.

questions.prompt: Why should an internal service-to-service API gateway avoid sharing a single database schema across independent bounded contexts?

options.text: SQL joins fail across schemas
Shared schemas create tight deployment coupling and prevent independent scaling or schema evolution
Database backups cannot include multiple tables
ORMs only support one table per service

questions.explanation: Shared databases turn microservices into a distributed monolith where any schema change risks breaking unrelated services.

questions.prompt: Your payment API experiences occasional 30-second spikes from a downstream fraud provider. Outline the resilience architecture (timeouts, circuit breaker, bulkhead, fallback) you would introduce and the business trade-offs.
questions.explanation: A resilient design bounds latency with strict timeouts, isolates thread/connection pools via bulkheads, trips circuit breakers on sustained failure, and defines explicit fail-open vs fail-closed risk policy.

rubric.label: Applies timeouts, bulkheads, and circuit breakers

questions.prompt: Compare using a Redis write-through cache vs cache-aside for a high-read product catalog with infrequent price updates, including invalidation and thundering-herd mitigation.
questions.explanation: Cache-aside fits read-heavy workloads well when paired with explicit invalidation on writes, jittered TTLs, and single-flight/request coalescing to prevent cache stampedes.

questions.prompt: P50 API latency is 40ms, but P99 jumped from 180ms to 3.4s after a release. What is the most effective first diagnostic step?

options.text: Increase P50 alerting threshold
Inspect distributed traces and flamegraphs filtered specifically to P99 slow requests
Restart all pods without capturing telemetry
Add more frontend CSS minification

questions.explanation: Tail latency spikes are invisible in averages/P50; sampling P99 traces immediately isolates lock contention, GC pauses, or N+1 downstream calls.

rubric.label: Avoids blind restarts that destroy evidence

questions.prompt: A Node.js API service shows 100% single-core CPU and rising event-loop lag whenever a large JSON report is requested. What is the root cause?

options.text: Too many async I/O promises
Synchronous CPU-bound work blocking the single-threaded event loop
Insufficient DNS TTL
HTTP/2 header compression

questions.explanation: Heavy synchronous serialization/computation starves the Node.js event loop; offload to worker threads, streaming, or background jobs.

questions.prompt: When implementing client retries against a degraded downstream service, why is exponential backoff paired with full jitter essential?

options.text: It guarantees zero failed requests
It desynchronizes retry storms so recovering servers are not overwhelmed simultaneously
It disables TCP keep-alive
It halves TLS handshake size

questions.explanation: Without jitter, synchronized client retries create periodic traffic waves (retry storms) that prolong outages.

questions.prompt: Select ALL valid SLO / Error Budget practices for production reliability engineering.

options.text: Define SLIs around user-perceived availability and latency
Freeze non-critical feature launches when error budget is exhausted
Target 100.000% uptime for every internal tool
Use multi-window burn-rate alerts to detect fast budget depletion

questions.explanation: 100% uptime is unrealistic and stalls innovation; SLIs, error budgets, and burn-rate alerts balance velocity and reliability.

rubric.label: Uses burn-rate alerting over noisy static thresholds

questions.prompt: Implement `dedupeByKey(items, key)` that returns a new array keeping only the first occurrence of each distinct `item[key]` in O(n) time while preserving input order.
questions.hint: Use a Set to track seen keys in a single pass.
questions.explanation: A single pass with a Set achieves O(n) time and preserves first-seen order without mutating input.

rubric.label: Preserves first occurrence and input immutability

questions.prompt: A database connection pool is sized to 500 connections per pod across 20 pods (10,000 total) against a primary DB with 32 vCPUs. What is the likely consequence under load?

options.text: Linear 10x throughput gain
Severe context-switching thrashing and lock contention degrading DB throughput
Zero impact because idle connections cost nothing
Automatic horizontal sharding

questions.explanation: Excessive active DB connections cause CPU context-switching and memory exhaustion; use bounded pools plus a connection pooler like PgBouncer.

questions.prompt: As Incident Commander during a Sev-1 checkout outage, what is your primary responsibility?

options.text: Personally write and deploy the hotfix without telling anyone
Coordinate roles, protect focus, drive mitigation decisions, and ensure regular stakeholder updates
Conduct root-cause blame analysis during the outage
Wait for full RCA before rolling back a bad release

questions.explanation: The Incident Commander orchestrates mitigation and communication rather than becoming a bottleneck inside the debugger.

questions.prompt: A deployment 12 minutes ago correlates with a 40% spike in 500 errors. What is the fastest safe mitigation?

options.text: Spend 2 hours reproducing locally before acting
Execute the documented rollback/feature-flag kill switch and verify error rates drop
Delete production logs to free disk space
Scale up pods to mask the 500 errors

questions.explanation: Mitigate customer impact first via fast rollback or feature flag, then investigate root cause safely offline.

questions.prompt: What is the core objective of a blameless postmortem after a production incident?

options.text: Identify which engineer to penalize
Uncover systemic gaps in tooling, guards, and processes and assign concrete preventive action items
Hide the incident from leadership
Prove that the incident could never happen again

questions.explanation: Blameless postmortems foster psychological safety so teams surface real systemic causes and build durable guardrails.

questions.prompt: Draft a concise Sev-1 status update for executive stakeholders 20 minutes into a partial login outage where a rollback is currently in progress.
questions.explanation: Executive updates must state customer impact, current mitigation action, what is known/unknown, and the exact timestamp of the next update.

rubric.label: Gives clear mitigation status and next update cadence

questions.prompt: During an outage, two engineers propose conflicting fixes simultaneously in the incident channel. How should the Incident Commander handle this?

options.text: Let both deploy at once to see which works
Pause, evaluate risk and reversibility of each option in 2 minutes, pick one owner to execute, and log the decision
Escalate to the CEO to pick the SQL query
Close the channel until tomorrow

questions.explanation: Single-threaded decision-making avoids compounding failures from uncoordinated production changes.

questions.prompt: When reviewing a junior engineer's 800-line PR that mixes formatting changes, a refactor, and a bug fix, what is the best coaching approach?

options.text: Approve immediately to avoid slowing them down
Point out critical correctness/security issues first, and coach them on splitting future PRs into focused, reviewable units
Rewrite the entire PR yourself and force-push over their branch
Leave 40 nitpick comments on variable naming only

questions.explanation: Prioritizing high-leverage feedback and teaching PR hygiene builds lasting engineering autonomy.

questions.prompt: How should a Senior Engineer structure an Architecture Decision Record (ADR) for a team?

options.text: Only list the final chosen library name
Document context, decision, considered alternatives, consequences, and trade-offs
Write a 50-page specification after the project ends
Keep decisions verbal in Slack threads

questions.explanation: ADRs preserve the why behind decisions so future engineers understand constraints and trade-offs before reversing them.

questions.prompt: A mid-level engineer consistently misses edge cases in async code. Which mentoring intervention is most effective?

options.text: Remove them from backend tasks permanently
Pair-program on writing failure-mode test cases (timeouts, retries, race conditions) and introduce a lightweight PR checklist
Tell them to be more careful
Disable async/await across the codebase

questions.explanation: Pairing on systematic failure-mode testing builds transferable mental models rather than relying on memory.

rubric.label: Uses pairing to build mental models

questions.prompt: A teammate proposes introducing a brand-new NoSQL database solely for a 5,000-row configuration table when your team already runs PostgreSQL. Write your constructive design-review feedback.
questions.explanation: Constructive review focuses on operational overhead, team expertise, data size, and whether existing infrastructure already satisfies requirements.

questions.prompt: Which signal best distinguishes a blocking code review comment from a non-blocking suggestion?

options.text: Personal stylistic preference on brace placement
Correctness bug, data-loss risk, security vulnerability, or broken public contract
Disagreement over a minor helper function name
Preferring map over for-of loop

questions.explanation: Blocking comments should be reserved for defects, security/reliability risks, or architectural violations; style belongs in automated linters.
